source_ledger.title: Can LLMs Detect Benchmark Defects? A Meta-Benchmark from Benchmark Updates
source_ledger.verification_depth: full paper method, curation, evaluation, results, and appendix passages inspected
evidence_locations: pp. 1-2: research question and root-cause matching
pp. 3-4: version-diff ground truth and curation
pp. 4-6: verify-only/solve-then-verify and harness ablations
appendix: prompt and manual-verification procedures
verified_facts: Task Verification Bench uses author-acknowledged benchmark updates as defect ground truth.
The verifier receives original task artifacts and emits a binary verdict plus a natural-language defect diagnosis.
The study evaluates root-cause-matched recall and precision, with an LLM judge comparing the diagnosis to update-derived ground truth.
Its evaluation covers SWE-bench and two non-overlapping Terminal-Bench splits and compares model, pipeline, and harness-access conditions.
It does not require the verifier to produce an executable test that fails on a parent revision and passes on a fixed revision.
source_ledger.role_in_v2: closest direct prior and mandatory design baseline

source_ledger.title: BenchGuard: Who Guards the Benchmarks? Automated Auditing of LLM Agent Benchmarks
source_ledger.authors: Xinming Tu, Tianze Wang, Yingzhou Lu, Kexin Huang, Yuanhao Qu, and Sara Mostafavi
source_ledger.verification_depth: full HTML method, evaluation, results, limitations, and prompts inspected
evidence_locations: Sections 3.1-3.3: artifact stack, taxonomy, and six-phase verification protocol
Section 4: two benchmark evaluation and human/expert validation
Section 5: recall, precision, ensemble, and cost results
Appendix B: definition-level prompt templates
verified_facts: BenchGuard cross-verifies instructions, reference programs, evaluation logic, and environments using structured LLM protocols and deterministic checks.
Its definition-level audit uses a six-phase structured reasoning protocol and emits evidence-linked findings rather than executable reproducers.
It evaluates on ScienceAgentBench and BIXBench with author-confirmed or expert-revised issues.
It uses human or expert adjudication and an alignment judge to validate findings.
source_ledger.role_in_v2: closest structured-audit prior and mandatory auditor baseline source

source_ledger.title: Automated Benchmark Auditing for AI Agents and Large Language Models
source_ledger.authors: Junlin Wang, Federico Bianchi, Shang Zhu, Fan Nie, Yongchan Kwon, Bhuwan Dhingra, and James Zou
source_ledger.verification_depth: full HTML method, portfolio, validation, reproducibility, and limitations inspected
evidence_locations: Section 2: evidence collector and static/trajectory auditor
Section 3: 168-benchmark portfolio and static audit
Section 4: upstream-PR and expert validation
Appendix C: pinned agent configuration and audit prompts
verified_facts: ABA normalizes heterogeneous benchmark artifacts into a manifest and uses a benchmark-agnostic agentic auditor.
Its outputs are structured issue findings with evidence paths and suggested fixes.
It validates findings against upstream pull requests, prior reports, and expert review.
It does not compare equal-budget executable test-generation procedures on parent/fixed evaluator revisions.
source_ledger.role_in_v2: large-scale benchmark-agnostic audit prior and reviewer-absorption threat

source_ledger.title: Establishing Best Practices for Building Rigorous Agentic Benchmarks
source_ledger.verification_depth: official proceedings PDF method, checklist, case studies, and appendices inspected
evidence_locations: pp. 2-6: task validity, outcome validity, and ABC checklist
pp. 7-9: ten-benchmark assessment and newly identified issues
Appendix F: benchmark-specific validation experiments
verified_facts: ABC defines task-validity and outcome-validity checks for agentic benchmarks.
The authors assess ten open-source agentic benchmarks and validate selected issues with benchmark-specific experiments.
The contribution is a checklist, assessment, and repair case study rather than an automated executable-reproducer comparison.
source_ledger.role_in_v2: domain framing, issue taxonomy, and validity criteria

source_ledger.title: UTBoost: Rigorous Evaluation of Coding Agents on SWE-Bench
source_ledger.authors: Boxi Yu, Yuxuan Zhu, Pinjia He, and Daniel Kang
source_ledger.verification_depth: official ACL Anthology PDF method, evaluation, results, and limitations inspected
evidence_locations: Sections 3-4: UTGenerator and UTBoost
Sections 5-6: test insufficiency and leaderboard correction results
verified_facts: UTBoost augments SWE-bench evaluation with LLM-generated unit tests.
It reports 36 task instances with insufficient tests and 345 erroneous patches that the original evaluation labeled as passed.
Its object is patch correctness within SWE-bench, not historical implementation faults in evaluator code across independent agent-evaluation repositories.
source_ledger.role_in_v2: mandatory test-generation prior and direct-example-regression baseline source

source_ledger.title: MR-Coupler: Automated Metamorphic Test Generation via Functional Coupling Analysis
source_ledger.authors: Congying Xu, Hengcheng Zhu, Songqiang Chen, Jiarong Wu, Valerio Terragni, and Shing-Chi Cheung
source_ledger.verification_depth: full HTML method, datasets, baselines, results, ablations, and threats inspected
evidence_locations: Section 3: functional-coupling method and generated metamorphic tests
Section 4.1: human-written tests and 50 real-world bugs
Sections 4.3-4.5: baseline and ablation results
Section 4.9: threats to validity
verified_facts: MR-Coupler uses functional coupling to generate and validate metamorphic tests.
Its evaluation includes 100 human-written metamorphic-test tasks and 50 real-world bugs.
It reports that generated metamorphic tests detect 44 percent of the 50 real bugs.
It does not focus on agent-evaluator contracts or compare structured contract relations with equal-information audit-to-reproducer procedures.

source_ledger.title: Evaluating Diverse Large Language Models for Automatic and General Bug Reproduction
source_ledger.authors: Sungmin Kang, Juyeon Yoon, Nargiz Askarbekkyzy, and Shin Yoo
source_ledger.verification_depth: full HTML approach, evaluation, results, and discussion inspected
evidence_locations: Section 3: bug-report-to-test pipeline
Sections 4-6: Defects4J evaluation and model comparisons
Section 7: limitations and failure analysis
verified_facts: LIBRO prompts LLMs with natural-language bug reports to generate bug-reproducing tests and ranks candidates through post-processing.
Its evaluation uses general software bugs rather than agent-evaluator implementation contracts.
It does not use a blinded parent-only comparison of multiple equal-budget test-authoring procedures.

source_ledger.title: An Empirical Evaluation of Property-Based Testing in Python
source_ledger.verification_depth: author PDF method, corpus, mutation study, parameter sweep, and threats inspected
evidence_locations: pp. 1-3: research questions and corpus
evaluation sections: mutation effectiveness and category comparison
parameter-sweep section: generated-input budget
verified_facts: The study categorizes property-based tests in 426 Python programs and evaluates suites from 40 projects with mutation testing.
Its evidence concerns mutation detection and existing test suites, not held-out historical evaluator faults or LLM-authored executable reproducers.

five_axis_comparison.research_object: Defective tasks in SWE-bench and Terminal-Bench versions
five_axis_comparison.core_question: Can LLM agents detect the correct root cause of benchmark defects?
five_axis_comparison.intervention_or_method: Verify-only or solve-then-verify diagnosis with optional harness access
five_axis_comparison.evaluation_unit_and_evidence: Task-level natural-language diagnosis matched to update-derived labels
five_axis_comparison.residual_difference: v2 requires an executable deterministic reproducer and compares authoring procedures under identical parent-only information and budgets.

five_axis_comparison.research_object: Coupled instruction, reference, evaluator, and environment artifacts in execution-based benchmarks
five_axis_comparison.core_question: Can structured LLM audits find benchmark defects missed by prior review?
five_axis_comparison.intervention_or_method: Six-phase cross-artifact audit plus deterministic checks
five_axis_comparison.evaluation_unit_and_evidence: Evidence-linked natural-language findings aligned to confirmed or expert-revised issues
five_axis_comparison.residual_difference: v2 converts parent-visible contracts into executable reproducers and tests whether that procedure adds detection value over an audit-first reproducer baseline.

five_axis_comparison.research_object: Tasks and artifacts across many LLM and agent benchmarks
five_axis_comparison.core_question: Can a benchmark-agnostic agent find instruction, environment, and evaluation issues at scale?
five_axis_comparison.intervention_or_method: Manifest normalization followed by static or trajectory audit
five_axis_comparison.evaluation_unit_and_evidence: Structured findings validated by reports, pull requests, or sampled expert review
five_axis_comparison.residual_difference: v2 studies controlled executable fault reproduction on a frozen historical parent/fix frame instead of open-ended issue reporting.

five_axis_comparison.research_object: Agentic benchmark validity and reporting practices
five_axis_comparison.core_question: Which validity checks should benchmark builders apply, and what failures do they expose?
five_axis_comparison.intervention_or_method: Checklist assessment plus issue-specific validation experiments
five_axis_comparison.evaluation_unit_and_evidence: Benchmark-level checklist scores and case-study measurements
five_axis_comparison.residual_difference: v2 evaluates automated test-authoring procedures rather than proposing a checklist.

five_axis_comparison.research_object: SWE-bench tasks and candidate agent patches
five_axis_comparison.core_question: Can generated tests correct insufficient patch evaluation?
five_axis_comparison.claim_scope: More rigorous evaluation of coding agents on SWE-bench
five_axis_comparison.residual_difference: v2 targets faults in evaluator implementations across repositories and compares four equal-budget authoring procedures with parent/fixed replay.

five_axis_comparison.research_object: General program methods, human metamorphic tests, and real software bugs
five_axis_comparison.core_question: Does functional coupling improve automated metamorphic-test generation?
five_axis_comparison.evaluation_unit_and_evidence: Valid test generation and bug detection
five_axis_comparison.residual_difference: v2 does not claim a new general metamorphic-testing method; it tests contract-structured authoring against direct audit and property-test procedures on agent-evaluator faults.

five_axis_comparison.research_object: General software bugs described by bug reports
five_axis_comparison.core_question: Can LLMs generate bug-reproducing tests from reports?
five_axis_comparison.intervention_or_method: Prompted test generation plus execution-based post-processing and ranking
five_axis_comparison.residual_difference: v2 uses parent-visible evaluator contracts, a held-out historical frame, controls, and equal-budget procedural comparison.

five_axis_comparison.core_question: How effective are property-based tests and their categories?
five_axis_comparison.intervention_or_method: Static categorization, mutation analysis, and input-budget sweep
five_axis_comparison.residual_difference: v2 evaluates generated tests on historical evaluator faults and clean controls rather than mutants.

subsumption_decision.surviving_research_question: Under equal parent-only information, model, tool, and execution budgets, does a structured contract-to-metamorphic-test procedure produce more independently replayable executable reproducers for historical agent-evaluator implementation faults than a prior-work-anchored audit-to-reproducer procedure, direct example regression, or free-form property-test generation?
subsumption_decision.surviving_contribution: A blinded cross-repository empirical comparison of executable-reproducer authoring procedures on historical agent-evaluator implementation faults.
forbidden_claims: Automated auditing of agent benchmarks is new.
Using LLMs to find benchmark defects is new.
Generating tests with LLMs is new.
Metamorphic testing finds real software bugs for the first time.
The retained frame estimates evaluator-defect prevalence in all agent benchmarks.
A structured prompt is a new general metamorphic-testing method.
subsumption_decision.strongest_reviewer_absorption_objection: Task Verification Bench, BenchGuard, and ABA already establish update-derived defect ground truth and structured LLM auditing, while UTBoost, LIBRO, and MR-Coupler already establish LLM-authored executable and metamorphic tests. A reviewer can therefore absorb v2 as a prompt-level recombination unless the study isolates executable-reproducer output, uses a prior-work-anchored audit-to-reproducer primary comparator, enforces information and budget parity, and demonstrates cross-cluster differences under deterministic parent/fixed replay.
automatic_kill_conditions: The prior-work-anchored auditor baseline cannot be implemented with the same parent-only information and budget as the structured arm.
The structured arm differs from the auditor baseline only in labels or prose without a distinct executable intermediate contract.
The historical frame cannot support source- and root-cause-independent deterministic parent/fixed replay.
The control corpus cannot estimate false alarms for all arms.
Any later primary source materially matches all five subsumption axes.
